```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#Loading necessary library
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(gtsummary)
library(pheatmap)
```

## Part 1: Data Cleaning

```{r, message=FALSE}
#Reading the Data into R --> using tidyverse

Covar          <- read_csv("GSE85307_covar-1.csv")
GeneExpression <- read_csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
GeneNames      <- read_csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")
```
```{r}
#initial sample sizes before cleaning
initial_covar_samples <- n_distinct(Covar$geoID)

# Gene expression samples are stored as columns (excluding PROBEID)
initial_expression_samples <- ncol(GeneExpression) - 1

initial_covar_samples
initial_expression_samples
```

```{r Cleaning-Age}
#picking out just the numeric in the age column.
Covar <- Covar %>%
  #mutate is used to add a column within the data set. 
  mutate(
    #str_remove is removing the "age_years: "
    mat_age_yrs = str_remove(mat_age_yrs, "^age_years:\\s*"),
    #as.numeric is specifying that the remaining value will be a number,not a character.
    mat_age_yrs = as.numeric(mat_age_yrs))

#making sure the cleaning created a numeric and removed the characters. 
head(Covar$mat_age_yrs)
class(Covar$mat_age_yrs)
```

```{r Cleaning All Variables}
#Continuing with remaining variables. 

#Condition
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    preg_preeclampsia = str_remove(preg_preeclampsia,"^pregnancy_condition:\\s*"),
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia))
#Delivery
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    delivery_gestAge_wks = str_remove(delivery_gestAge_wks, "^gestation_weeks:\\s*"),
    delivery_gestAge_wks = as.numeric(delivery_gestAge_wks))
#Sample Collection
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    sampleCollection_gestAge_wks = str_remove(sampleCollection_gestAge_wks,
      "^blood_draw_at_gestation_week:\\s*"),
    sampleCollection_gestAge_wks =
      as.numeric(sampleCollection_gestAge_wks))
#Batch MicroArray
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    batch_Microarray = str_remove(batch_Microarray,
      "^microarray_hybridization_date:\\s*"),
    batch_Microarray = as.factor(batch_Microarray))
#BMI
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    mat_BMI = str_remove(mat_BMI, "^bmi_kg/m2:\\s*"),
    mat_BMI = as.numeric(mat_BMI))
#Vitamin D
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    mat_vitD = str_remove(mat_vitD,
      "^vitamind_25\\(0h\\)_ng/ml_whole_blood_baseline:\\s*"),
    mat_vitD = as.numeric(mat_vitD))
#Asthma
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    mat_asthma = str_remove(mat_asthma, "asthma_0=healthy_1=asthmatic:\\s*"),
    mat_asthma = as.factor(mat_asthma))
```

```{r}
#deriving categories from a continuous variable - BMI
Covar <- Covar %>%
      mutate(
        BMI_category = cut(
        mat_BMI,
        #breaks indicate BMI values cutoffs for each category (Inf stand in for below and above)
        breaks = c(-Inf, 18.5, 25, 30, Inf),
        #Labels match the breaks indicated above. standard BMI cutoffs.  
        labels = c(
            "Underweight",
            "Normal weight",
            "Overweight",
            "Obesity"),
        right = FALSE))
# Check the new BMI categories
Covar %>%
count(BMI_category)
```

```{r}
#Summary of Cleaned Variables. 
head(Covar %>% select(mat_age_yrs, preg_preeclampsia, delivery_gestAge_wks, sampleCollection_gestAge_wks,
                      batch_Microarray, mat_BMI, mat_vitD, mat_asthma))
```

```{r}
# Check the first few sample IDs in the gene expression data
names(GeneExpression)[1:10]
# Check the geoID values in the covariate data
head(Covar$geoID)
# Check the first column of the gene expression data
head(GeneExpression[[1]])
```


```{r}
#Our first column is unnamed, so we will identify it. It is the PROBEID 
#assignments for the genes.  
GeneExpression <- GeneExpression %>%
  rename(PROBEID = 1)

#we want to extract the geoID from both csv files. 
covar_ids <- Covar$geoID
# [-1] is excluding the first column, ProbeID as it is not a gene column
expression_ids <- names(GeneExpression)[-1]

# Count how many sample IDs match
# %in% is asking is the geoID from covar_ids is named in expression_ids
#TRUE means a match and will contribute to the sum. 
sum(covar_ids %in% expression_ids)

#Check whether any covariate sample IDs are missing from gene expression
#should be zero as we want all to be matched.
setdiff(covar_ids, expression_ids)

# Check how many gene-expression sample IDs match the covariate data
sum(expression_ids %in% covar_ids)
```

```{r}
#selecting a gene to observe. 
#we are looking for the PROBEID that goes along with selected gene. WIPI2
My_ProbeID <- GeneNames %>%
  filter(GENE == "WIPI2") %>%
  #pull is used to extract just the probeid from the gene we want 
  pull(PROBEID) #pulling from the column looking just for WIPI2
```

```{r}
# Extract expression values for the selected gene
WIPI2 <- GeneExpression %>%
  #from GeneExpression we was to filter all the observations of WIPI2 which is My_ProbeID
  filter(PROBEID %in% My_ProbeID)
  #gives a new data set with just WIPI2 variables. 

# Change the data from wide format to long format to change from one observation to 157 observations. 
# Each row will represent one sample or observation. 
WIPI2_long <- WIPI2 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    #cols will remove the PROBEID column as its not needed
    cols = -PROBEID,
    names_to = "geoID",
    values_to = "gene_expression")

# Match gene expression to participant information using geoID
#Plotdata will be used to plot WIPI2, and its going to have just WIPI2_long and the 12 patient covariates. 
PlotData <- Covar %>%
  #inner_join is used almost like mutate, to join the geoID col to my WIPI2_long dataset. 
  inner_join(WIPI2_long, by = "geoID")
```

# Part 2: First Gene Plots

### Histogram of WIPI2 Gene Expression

```{r}
#ggplot required
#x is our gene_expression value which is a numeric.
ggplot(PlotData, aes(x = gene_expression))+
geom_histogram(
  #bins are used to change how thick the histogram bars are. 
      bins = 20,
      #fill is for filling the color of the histogram bars. 
      fill = "purple",
      #color here is for between the bins to tell our towers apart. 
      color = "white") +
    labs(
        title = expression("Distribution of " * italic("WIPI2") * " Gene Expression"),
        x = expression(italic("WIPI2") * " Gene Expression"),
        y = "Number of Participants",
        caption = paste("Figure 1. Distribution of WIPI2 gene expression among",
                  "157 maternal samples.\n","Bars represent the number of",
                  "participants within each gene-expression interval.")) +
theme_classic() +
    theme(
        plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 10,
        #0 indicates alignment to the left. 
        hjust = 0))
```

```{r}
#Scatter plot of maternal age and gene_expression
ggplot(PlotData, aes(x = mat_age_yrs, y = gene_expression)) +
  geom_point(
    color = "purple",
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE,
    color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = expression("Maternal Age and " * italic(WIPI2) * " Gene Expression"),
    x = "Maternal Age (years)",
    y = expression(italic("WIPI2") * " Gene Expression"),
  caption = paste("Figure 2. Association between maternal age and WIPI2 gene expression.",
                "Each point represents one\n", "participant. The black line represents",
                "the fitted linear regression, and the gray region represents the\n",
                "95% confidence interval.")) +
  theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0),
      plot.caption.position = "plot")
```

```{r}
# Box plot of WIPI2 gene expression by pregnancy outcome and BMI category
ggplot(PlotData, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = gene_expression)) +
      geom_boxplot(
        fill = "purple",
        alpha = 0.6,
        na.rm = TRUE) +
#geom_jitter used to represent data better by showing amount of data points. 
      geom_jitter(
        width = 0.2,
        alpha = 0.4,
        na.rm = TRUE) +
  #facet_wrap used to create panels for the categoricals. 
      facet_wrap(~ BMI_category) +
      labs(
            title = expression(italic("WIPI2") * " Gene Expression by Pregnancy Outcome and BMI Category"),
            x = "Pregnancy Outcome",
            y = expression(italic("WIPI2") * " Gene Expression"),
            caption = paste("Figure 3. WIPI2 gene expression by pregnancy outcome and maternal BMI category.", "Boxes represent\n", "the interquartile range, center lines indicate medians, and whiskers show the spread of the data.\n", "BMI categories were derived from maternal BMI.")) +
      theme_classic() +
        theme(
        plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 10,
        hjust = 0),
      plot.caption.position = "plot")
```

# Part 3: Function for Future Plots

```{r}
#creating a data frame that holds our covariate and categoricals. 
#Convert gene expression data from wide to long format
GeneExpression_long <- GeneExpression %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -PROBEID,
    names_to = "geoID",
    values_to = "gene_expression")
#combing the three data sets
CombinedData <- GeneExpression_long %>%
  inner_join(GeneNames, by = "PROBEID") %>%
  inner_join(Covar, by = "geoID")

#Final sample size for reference
final_sample_size <- n_distinct(CombinedData$geoID)
final_participant_size <- n_distinct(CombinedData$subjectID)

final_sample_size
final_participant_size
```

```{r}
# Count missing values in each covariate
Missing_Data <- Covar %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Missing_Count")
```


```{r}
#Function Creation
Gene_Plot_Function <- function(data,
                               genes,
                               continuous_var,
                               categorical_vars) {

  #Identify the probe IDs for the selected genes
  My_ProbeIDs <- data %>%
    filter(GENE %in% genes) %>%
    distinct(GENE, PROBEID)

  #Extract gene expression data for the selected genes
  PlotData <- data %>%
    inner_join(My_ProbeIDs, by = c("GENE", "PROBEID"))

  #Create an empty list to store all plots
  All_Plots <- list()
  
  #incorporating feedback by creating a color palette (I want my pickle green!)
  my.gene.palette <- c("firebrick", "forestgreen", "steelblue", "purple", "darkorange")

  #Loop through the plotting instructions for each gene
  for (i in seq_along(genes)) {
    gene <- genes[i]
    gene_color <- my.gene.palette[i]

    #One gene at a time
    GeneData <- PlotData %>%
      filter(GENE == gene)

    #HISTOGRAM: Distribution of gene expression
    Histogram <- ggplot(GeneData, aes(x = gene_expression)) +
      geom_histogram(
        bins = 20,
        fill = gene_color,
        color = "white") +
      labs(
        #bquote introduced instead of paste to incorporate "italic"
        title = bquote("Distribution of " * italic(.(gene)) * " Gene Expression"),
        x = bquote(italic(.(gene)) * " Gene Expression"),
        y = "Number of Participants") +
      theme_classic()

    #SCATTERPLOT: Maternal age and gene expression
    Scatterplot <- ggplot(GeneData, aes(x = .data[[continuous_var]], y = gene_expression)) +
      geom_point(
        color = gene_color,
        alpha = 0.5,
        size = 2) +
      geom_smooth(
        method = "lm",
        se = TRUE,
        color = "black") +
      labs(
        title = bquote("Maternal Age and " * italic(.(gene)) * " Gene Expression"),
        x = "Maternal Age (years)",
        y = bquote(italic(.(gene)) * " Gene Expression")) +
      theme_classic()

    #BOXPLOT: Gene expression by pregnancy outcome and BMI category
    Boxplot <- ggplot(GeneData, aes(x = .data[[categorical_vars[1]]], y = gene_expression)) +
      geom_boxplot(
        fill = gene_color,
        alpha = 0.6,
        na.rm = TRUE) +
      geom_jitter(
        width = 0.2,
        alpha = 0.4,
        na.rm = TRUE) +
      #creates a separate panel for each BMI category
      facet_wrap(vars(.data[[categorical_vars[2]]])) +
      labs(
        title = bquote(italic(.(gene)) * " Gene Expression by Pregnancy Outcome and BMI Category"),
        x = "Pregnancy Outcome",
        y = bquote(italic(.(gene)) * " Gene Expression")) +
      theme_classic()

    #Store the three plots for each gene
    All_Plots[[gene]] <- list(
      Histogram = Histogram,
      Scatterplot = Scatterplot,
      Boxplot = Boxplot)

    #Display the three plots
    print(Histogram)
    print(Scatterplot)
    print(Boxplot)
  }
  #Return all plots
  return(All_Plots)
}
```


```{r}
JAM2_PRICKLE2_Plots <- Gene_Plot_Function(
  data = CombinedData,
  genes = c("JAM2", "PRICKLE2"),
  continuous_var = "mat_age_yrs",
  categorical_vars = c("preg_preeclampsia", "BMI_category"))
```

# Part 4: Sample Data Table

```{r}
# Create summary statistics table stratified by pregnancy outcome
Summary_Table <- Covar %>%
  select(
    mat_age_yrs,
    mat_BMI,
    mat_vitD,
    BMI_category,
    preg_preeclampsia) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = preg_preeclampsia,
    label = list(
      mat_age_yrs ~ "Maternal Age (years)",
      mat_BMI ~ "Maternal BMI (kg/m²)",
      mat_vitD ~ "Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)",
      BMI_category ~ "BMI Category"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 2,)

Summary_Table
```

# Part 4: Heat Map

```{r}
# Select 10 genes for the heatmap
#selected based on there siginificane in the health of placenta during pregnancy
Heatmap_Genes <- c(
  "WIPI2",
  "JAM2",
  "PRICKLE2",
  "PLAC4",
  "IGFBP1",
  "TIMP1",
  "NODAL",
  "VIT",
  "CDH2",
  "MEST")

#making sure PROBEID exist for all 10 genes
Heatmap_ProbeIDs <- GeneNames %>%
  filter(GENE %in% Heatmap_Genes) %>%
  distinct(GENE, PROBEID) %>%
  arrange(match(GENE, Heatmap_Genes))
```

```{r}
#New Data set for just the heat maps 10 genes. 
Heatmap_Data <- CombinedData %>%
  #using CombinedData as it has our covariates, gene_expression, geoID, and GENE.
  inner_join(Heatmap_ProbeIDs, by = c("GENE", "PROBEID")) %>%
  select(GENE, geoID, gene_expression) %>%
  #10 rows of genes, with 157 sample data in each column. 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = geoID,
    values_from = gene_expression)

#Matrix necessary for removing the gene name column, and making it the row name instead. 
#we now have 10 rows of 157 samples
Heatmap_Matrix <- Heatmap_Data %>%
  column_to_rownames("GENE") %>%
  as.matrix()
```

```{r}
heatmap_cats <- Covar %>%
  select(geoID, preg_preeclampsia, BMI_category) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  rename(
    `Preeclampsia Status` = preg_preeclampsia,
    `Maternal BMI Category` = BMI_category) %>%
  column_to_rownames("geoID")

# Match annotation order to heat map samples
heatmap_cats <- heatmap_cats[
  colnames(Heatmap_Matrix),]
```

```{r}
pheatmap(
  Heatmap_Matrix,
  scale = "row",
  annotation_col = heatmap_cats,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "complete",
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  fontsize_row = 10,
  labels_row = parse(text = paste0("italic('", rownames(Heatmap_Matrix), "')")),
  #removing the borders is necessary because we have 157 interpretations. 
  border_color = NA,
  main = "Gene Expression Patterns Across Samples")
```

# Part 5: Additional Plot

```{r}
Barplot_Data <- CombinedData %>%
  #filtering out our ten genes from the original data
  filter(GENE %in% Heatmap_Genes) %>%
  #we are looking at comparing pre-eclampsia conditions. 
  group_by(GENE, preg_preeclampsia) %>%
  summarise(
    #i want to look at mean gene expression for my ten genes. 
    mean_expression = mean(gene_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_expression = sd(gene_expression, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    se = sd_expression / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  Barplot_Data,
  aes(x = GENE, y = mean_expression, fill = preg_preeclampsia)) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7) +
  #this is used for formatting the extraced gene names. 
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) parse(text = paste0("italic('", x, "')"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Gene Expression by Pregnancy Outcome",
    x = "Gene",
    y = "Mean Gene Expression",
    fill = "Pregnancy Outcome") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
